He could train hard. He knew what he should be doing.

But outside the gym, things were very different.

Dan struggled badly with anxiety and often turned to alcohol for that short-term escape. The drinking affected his food, his progress disappeared, he’d feel worse… and the cycle would start again.

Train. Progress. Undo it. Start again.

title: I spent 4 years making fitness WAY more complicated than it needed to be.
hook: I spent 4 years making fitness WAY more complicated than it needed to be.
caption:
I spent 4 years making fitness WAY more complicated than it needed to be.

Here are the 5 things that actually moved the needle:

1. Train harder.

The perfect exercise selection means nothing if your sets aren’t challenging you. Good execution + progressive overload + training close to failure built far more muscle for me than constantly changing my workouts.

2. Eat with intention.

Your diet doesn’t need to be chicken and rice 6x a day. Hit your protein, understand your calories, eat mostly quality foods and make your diet something you can actually stick to.

3. Prioritize recovery.

caption:
Can you guess my body-fat percentage? I can't—and I don't really care.

Earlier in my training career, I cared a lot more about the number.

I'd use body-fat scanners and scales, then compare myself to pictures online trying to figure out: Am I 12%? 10%? 8%? 6%?

After more than 15 years of natural bodybuilding, getting extremely lean several times, and competing, I've learned that the number matters a lot less than people think.

Because what are you actually trying to accomplish?
